mathSemantics.problemFamily: inclusive finite sums of a univariate rational-coefficient polynomial
mathSemantics.statement: Let p be a univariate polynomial in k with rational coefficients and constant denominators only, and let a, b be integers with b >= a - 1 and |a|, |b| <= 10^6. Construct G in the same class such that G(k+1) - G(k) = p(k) as polynomials. If that identity is independently checked, the inclusive sum from k = a to k = b of p(k) equals G(b+1) - G(a), using the hand-provided telescoping infrastructure rule. The empty sum b = a - 1 is 0.

variables.p: univariate polynomial in the summation index; coefficients in Q; constant denominators only

necessaryConditions: p is a univariate QQ-polynomial in the summation variable
G(k+1)-G(k)=p(k) is independently checked as a polynomial identity
a and b are integers with b >= a - 1
degrees and coefficient sizes stay within the certificate checker limits
unsupportedInputs: extra parameters or free symbols besides the summation index
upper < lower - 1 (reversed bounds; not Karr's negative sum)
hypergeometric terms the polynomial checker cannot verify

restrictedInputs.summand: expression string in the Math Anchor safe_expression polynomial subset
restrictedInputs.antidifference: optional candidate G in the same language; omitted means construct via Gosper

outputs.value: exact rational fraction payload when the identity is checked and bounds are in domain
outputs.verification: obligation status, checker id/version, certificate digest

verification.note: Never mark formal_kernel_checked. Lean is not used. A few in-scope instances are not a proof for every polynomial.

novelty.details: Gosper's algorithm and Faulhaber's formula for polynomial powers are classical. SymPy already constructs G and sums the value. Math Anchor already checks rational polynomial identities with constant denominators. This pack is an experimental retrieve/instantiate wrapper around that existing chain. The telescoping combination rule is A1 infrastructure and is not Agent-extracted novelty.
